experiment_name: Acid Chloride Synthesis with Thionyl Chloride
experiment_description: Preparation of an acid chloride from a carboxylic acid using thionyl chloride, based on the protocol for 2-Methoxy-4-(1-Boc-4-piperidyloxy)benzoyl chloride. ChloroaceticAcid is used as the representative carboxylic acid substrate. Required instruments: RoundBottomFlask, HeatingPlate, RotaryEvaporator, ElectronicScale. Required reagents: ChloroaceticAcid, ThionylChloride, Tetrahydrofuran, Pyridine, DiethylEther.

assets.name: ThionylChloride
assets.purpose: Chlorinating agent to convert acid to acid chloride

assets.name: Pyridine
assets.purpose: Catalyst and base to neutralize HCl

procedure.description: Retrieve ChloroaceticAcid, ThionylChloride, Tetrahydrofuran, Pyridine, and DiethylEther from ReagentCabinet and place them in the FumeHood (liquids) and ExperimentalPlatform (solids).
procedure.safety_notes: Handle ThionylChloride and Pyridine with extreme care; ensure FumeHood is active.

procedure.description: Weigh ChloroaceticAcid using the ElectronicScale and transfer it into a Beaker.
procedure.safety_notes: Avoid contact with solid acid; wear gloves.

procedure.description: Transfer ChloroaceticAcid to a RoundBottomFlask in the FumeHood and dissolve in Tetrahydrofuran using a Pipette.
procedure.safety_notes: Perform in FumeHood due to solvent vapors.

procedure.description: Add a catalytic amount of Pyridine to the mixture, then add ThionylChloride dropwise while stirring with the HeatingPlate (stirring function).
procedure.safety_notes: Exothermic reaction; gas evolution (HCl, SO2). Keep sash low.

procedure.description: Stir the reaction mixture at ambient temperature for 4.5 hours to ensure conversion to acid chloride.
procedure.safety_notes: Monitor for consistent stirring; ensure ventilation.

procedure.description: Transfer the RoundBottomFlask to the RotaryEvaporator to remove Tetrahydrofuran and excess ThionylChloride under reduced pressure.
procedure.safety_notes: Collect waste solvents in appropriate waste container; trap acidic vapors.

procedure.description: Redissolve the residue in DiethylEther in the FumeHood to wash/precipitate impurities.
procedure.safety_notes: DiethylEther is extremely flammable; ensure no ignition sources.

procedure.description: Concentrate the solution again using the RotaryEvaporator to obtain the final acid chloride product.
procedure.safety_notes: Ensure vacuum system is protected from corrosive vapors.

procedure.description: Transfer a sample of the product to the ValidationPlatform for analysis using the LiquidChromatograph.
procedure.safety_notes: Handle product as a corrosive acid chloride.

safety_warnings: Thionyl Chloride is highly toxic and reacts violently with water; use only in a well-ventilated FumeHood.
Tetrahydrofuran and Diethyl Ether are peroxide-forming flammable solvents; check for peroxides before use.
Acid chlorides are corrosive and lachrymatory; avoid all skin and eye contact.
notes: ChloroaceticAcid is used as a model substrate because 2-Methoxy-4-(1-Boc-4-piperidyloxy)benzoic acid is not available in the library. The procedure follows the standard thionyl chloride activation protocol.
